status_summary: The three outreach offices were placed under deputy chiefs of staff other than the Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy. White House announcements of 2025-02-19 say the Intergovernmental Affairs and Political Affairs offices report to Deputy Chief of Staff James Blair, whose portfolio Axios describes as legislative, political and public affairs, and a 2025-01-24 announcement placed Public Liaison, Communications and Cabinet Affairs under Taylor Budowich, Deputy Chief of Staff for Communications and Public Liaison. Stephen Miller was named deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security advisor, and Reuters described him in that role in July 2025. Axios reported on 2025-09-24 that Budowich would leave at the end of September 2025, and on 2026-04-10 that Blair was considering a leave to run the President's outside political operation for the midterms; Voz.us reported the same day that the President announced a short leave of absence for Blair. No reassignment of the three offices to the policy deputy was found.

timeline.event: The White House announces Public Liaison, Communications and Cabinet Affairs appointments, saying those offices will be overseen by the Deputy Chief of Staff for Communications and Public Liaison, who is also designated Cabinet Secretary.
The White House announces Intergovernmental Affairs appointments and says the office reports to Assistant to the President and Deputy Chief of Staff James Blair, not the policy deputy.
The White House announces Office of Political Affairs appointments and says the office also reports to Deputy Chief of Staff James Blair.

Axios reports that the deputy chief of staff overseeing communications, public liaison, cabinet affairs and speechwriting plans to leave at the end of September 2025; the report does not name a successor.

Axios reports that Deputy Chief of Staff for Legislative, Political and Public Affairs James Blair is considering a leave to help run the President's outside political operation for the midterms; Voz.us reports the President announced a short leave of absence. Neither report says who covers his offices.

title: Consider placing IGA, Political Affairs and Public Liaison under the policy deputy chief
uncertainties: The reporting lines of Intergovernmental Affairs, Political Affairs and Public Liaison come from three White House announcements read on whitehouse.gov; those announcements name Blair as deputy chief of staff without a portfolio, which comes from Axios. The policy deputy's title comes from an NPR report of November 2024 and a Reuters report of July 2025. Whether Blair's leave took effect, who covered his offices, and who took over Budowich's offices were not confirmed; current reporting lines after these departures are unknown. The chapter frames the arrangement as one that could help, and pages 33 to 34 leave reporting lines to the Chief of Staff, so the diverged stage records that the structure differs from an optional suggestion, not that a firm recommendation was rejected.
